<!-- Generated by Kora's design director. This is the design decision the site was built
     from. Business: DRY EYECARE -->

# DESIGN.md — DRY EYECARE

archetype: practice-warm
rationale: Dry eye patients usually reach Dr. Inna Lazar after months of drops that stopped working, tired and sceptical, so DRY EYECARE needs a calm, short page that makes one clear promise (relief that relies far less on drops), puts the doctor behind it, and carries itself on deep teal, pale aqua and type alone because there is no photography.
interaction_level: L1

personality: [reassuring, clear, quietly modern, kind]

typography:
  display: "Karla"
  body: "Karla"
  scale: 1.25
  notes: |
    Karla is the only family on the page. This keeps the page honest to the brand and to practice-warm's warm sans body.
    - **Headings:** 700 weight. The hero phrase is around 4.5rem on desktop, section headings around 2.25rem, and the service name around 1.6rem.
    - **Body:** 400 weight at a generous 1.125rem, with a 1.65 line-height and a measure capped near 62ch.
    - **Lead paragraphs:** set at 1.375rem in 400, so the explanation reads as speech rather than small print.
    - **Eyebrows:** 0.8125rem, 700, uppercase, with 0.08em tracking. Nothing on the page goes smaller.
    - **Form labels:** full body size in 700, never tiny grey hints.

palette:
  primary: "#0d3c39"
  secondary: "#06211f"
  accent: "#b0f5f9"
  ground: "#f4f2ec"
  surface: "#e4ece8"
  ink: "#112b29"
  muted: "#4b615e"
  border: "#c8d3cf"
  application: |
    - **Primary (#0d3c39):** carries the hero panel and the closing enquiry band as full-width blocks. This gives the page two deep-teal moments of real weight rather than one coloured button.
    - **Secondary (#06211f):** grounds the footer and the hover state of primary actions.
    - **Accent (#b0f5f9):** used only on primary or secondary grounds.
      - It sets the emphasised word in the hero.
      - It fills the submit button, with secondary-teal text on accent.
      - It draws the focus rings inside dark bands.
      - It is never text or a fill on the light ground, where it would vanish.
    - **Ground (#f4f2ec):** the page sits on a warm paper.
    - **Surface (#e4ece8):** a pale teal-grey tint for the service block and the story's aside.
    - **Ink (#112b29):** the brand teal pushed nearly to black.
    - **Muted (#4b615e):** a desaturated brand teal that clears 4.5:1 on both ground and surface.
    - **Why these neutrals:** the paper is warm so the teal reads as care rather than clinic, and every neutral is drawn from the teal itself, so nothing on the page is stock grey.

composition:
  whitespace: generous
  photography: none
  card_usage: minimal
  mobile: |
    - **Hero:** the headline drops from around 4.5rem to around 2.6rem. The teal panel stays full-bleed and keeps its weight.
    - **Story:** becomes a single column, with the surface-tinted aside following the main text.
    - **Form:** fields go full width with a 48px minimum tap target, and the submit button goes full width.
    - **No sticky bar:** there is no phone number to call.

composition: |
  Lead with the promise in their own words, drop-less relief, and with the doctor behind it. Patients who have tried everything need to hear that a specialist will evaluate them properly and build a plan before they are shown any treatment name.

  The single treatment, OptiLIGHT, comes second, explained plainly as the "why it works". The page ends by handing them a gentle way to start that conversation.

  The one memorable moment is the hero: "Drop-less" set very large in pale aqua against the deep teal panel, with a single soft arc rule beneath the headline like the line of an eyelid.

  Keep the whole page short. Its brevity is part of the calm.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      - State what this is, using "DRY EYECARE" and the tagline verbatim: "Drop-less dry eye treatment in Greenwich & Darien, CT".
      - Let a drop-weary visitor feel at once that this is a specialist practice offering a different route.
      - Include one action that scrolls to the enquiry form.
  - id: story
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      - Introduce Dr. Inna Lazar as founder of PRO EYECARE, drawing only on the description.
      - Explain the approach in plain language: a dedicated dry eye evaluation first, then a plan built around in-office treatments that restore the eyelid oil glands, so patients can rely far less on drops.
      - Write it as prose. No numbered steps.
  - id: offerings
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      - Title the section "Services" or "Treatment", never "Menu".
      - Present OptiLIGHT as the single in-office treatment, with its description verbatim.
      - Give one service real presence rather than pretending to a list.
      - Show no price and no duration, because none exist.
  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: |
      - Give the visitor a gentle, human way to start, via an enquiry form posting to Kora.
        - Use form_type "contact".
        - Load reCAPTCHA lazily.
      - Collect name, email and message, plus phone only if the visitor offers it.
      - Use a warm button label such as "Ask about an evaluation". Never "Submit", and never "Call us", since no phone number exists.
      - Show no address, phone or email, because none are available.

avoid:
  - A "Call us" button or tel: link. No phone number exists, so the default CTA label must not be used.
  - Eye-drop or water-droplet icons, eyeball clip-art, and anatomical eye diagrams as decoration.
  - Any invented detail beyond the tagline's town names:
    - an address or map
    - opening hours
    - a phone number or email
    - a "two convenient locations" block
  - Inventing anything to fill out the Services section: extra treatments, prices, session counts, success rates, or before/after claims.
  - Testimonials, star ratings, "trusted by" lines, or credential badges. None exist.
  - Clinical jargon in headings. "Meibomian gland dysfunction" belongs in the body, not a headline.
  - Accent #b0f5f9 used as text or a button on the light paper ground.
  - Pure white backgrounds, pure black text, and grey stock neutrals.
  - A three-card "Evaluate / Treat / Relief" icon row, or 01/02/03 numbering.
  - A wall of text in the story. Short paragraphs, one idea each.
  - A newsletter signup. Nothing in the content calls for one.
